name: Kisspeptin-10

b.x: Within 30 minutes of an IV dose, serum LH climbs sharply in healthy men. That speed is what makes kisspeptin-10 (KP10, amino acids 112 to 121 of the KISS1 gene product, MW ~1,302 Da) unusual among reproductive peptides. It sits at the very top of the HPG axis, binding the KISS1R (GPR54) receptor on GnRH neurons to trigger downstream gonadotropin release. George and colleagues (J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2011) [1] gave healthy men IV boluses of kisspeptin-10. LH rose most at 1 mcg/kg, from 4.1 to 12.4 IU/L at 30 minutes, and less at 3 mcg/kg. Infusions lasting up to 22.5 hours raised testosterone and increased LH pulse frequency and size. A separate study [2] demonstrated sexual dimorphism in the response; women responded in the preovulatory phase but showed no gonadotropin change in the follicular phase. George and colleagues [3] extended this to men with type 2 diabetes and hypogonadism, where kisspeptin-10 still produced an acute LH rise. In practice, the community uses it primarily for two things: natural testosterone optimization and post-TRT HPTA restart. The typical protocol is 100 to 125 mcg subcutaneous nightly, cycled 30 days on and 30 days off. Forum presence is thin compared to BPC-157 or TB-500 but concentrated in specialist boards like ExcelMale. The honest limitation: no large randomized controlled trial has tested kisspeptin-10 for therapeutic hypogonadism. Post-TRT recovery application is biologically plausible but formally unstudied. Frequent or continuous dosing causes desensitization: twice-daily kisspeptin-54 in women [4] and continuous kisspeptin-10 infusion in men [6]. The peptide itself degrades faster than almost anything else on the market, with an in vitro plasma half-life of roughly 55 seconds.

Kisspeptin-10 is the minimal bioactive fragment of the KISS1 gene product. It binds with high affinity to KISS1R (GPR54), a G-protein coupled receptor sitting on GnRH neurons in the arcuate and anteroventral periventricular nuclei of the hypothalamus. Receptor activation triggers Gq/11 signaling. Intracellular calcium rises, protein kinase C activates, and the GnRH neuron depolarizes. The result is pulsatile GnRH secretion into the hypophyseal portal system at the median eminence, a region that lacks a complete blood-brain barrier. GnRH then hits gonadotroph cells in the anterior pituitary, releasing both LH and FSH. The LH pulse following an IV kisspeptin-10 bolus peaks at about 30 minutes [1] and returns to baseline within roughly 3 hours. In men, that LH spike drives Leydig cell testosterone production. In women, the magnitude depends on menstrual cycle phase; preovulatory timing produces the largest response. One detail that matters for long-term protocols: kisspeptin neurons also integrate metabolic signals from leptin, insulin, and ghrelin, plus photoperiod cues. They function as a gatekeeping node that couples energy status to reproductive output. Repeated or continuous exposure leads to GnRH neuron desensitization and reduced gonadotropin output. That property is actually being explored for endometriosis and precocious puberty, where suppression of the reproductive axis is the goal.
Kisspeptin-10 benefits center on upstream HPG axis stimulation and the body's own hormone production.
Stimulates LH release fast. In healthy men, an IV bolus of 1 mcg/kg raised LH from 4.1 to 12.4 IU/L at 30 minutes [1].

Raises testosterone through the endogenous pathway. Exogenous testosterone suppresses the hypothalamus and HCG bypasses it; kisspeptin-10 acts above both, which is why HPTA restart protocols use it. Continuous exposure can blunt this pathway (see Side Effects).
Raised LH in 5 men with type 2 diabetes and low testosterone (George et al.) [3]. An 11-hour infusion in 4 of them lifted testosterone from 8.5 to 11.4 nmol/L.

Studied as an IVF oocyte maturation trigger, but only as kisspeptin-54. In 60 women at high OHSS risk, none developed moderate or severe OHSS [5]. KP10 shares the KISS1R mechanism but has no trigger data.
A needle-free route is in testing, though with kisspeptin-54, not KP10. In a 2025 eBioMedicine trial [7], 12.8 nmol/kg intranasal kisspeptin-54 raised peak LH by a mean 4.4 IU/L in healthy men.
Community users consistently report improved morning erections, mood, and energy starting around days 5 to 10 of daily subcutaneous dosing.
Partially Aligned
Scientific Evidence
Based on 11 key studies · Research only
KP10 stimulates LH and FSH release in healthy men, and in women only in the preovulatory phase, via KISS1R → GnRH → pituitary axis.

Dosing studied: IV bolus in healthy men: 0.01–3.0 mcg/kg, with the largest LH rise in that range at 1 mcg/kg (PMID 21632807); 0.3–10 nmol/kg, with LH raised at doses as low as 0.3 nmol/kg (PMID 21976724); 100–200 mcg SC daily (community practice; no study converts the IV doses to an injection dose)

Proof-of-concept in T2DM hypogonadism [3]. Blunted response in severe iHH patients. Tachyphylaxis is documented with twice-daily kisspeptin-54 [4] and continuous kisspeptin-10 infusion [6]. Intranasal kisspeptin-54 raised LH in a 2025 trial [7]; KP10 has no intranasal data. No FDA-approved therapeutic indication; FDA has listed KP10 in 503A Category 2 since Sept 29, 2023.
Key Study
PMID 21632807: KP10 IV boluses raised LH in healthy men, most at 1 mcg/kg. Infusions up to 22.5 hours raised testosterone and LH pulse frequency and size (J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2011)
Limitations

No large RCTs for therapeutic hypogonadism endpoints. Post-TRT recovery application is community-only, not formally studied. In one IV study, 3 mcg/kg raised LH less than 1 mcg/kg (PMID 21632807). No human study has measured subcutaneous bioavailability or tested once-daily injections (FDA 2024 review). In follicular-phase women, single subcutaneous injections raised plasma kisspeptin but did not change LH (PMID 21976724). iHH patients show blunted response vs. healthy controls.
Community Experience
Used primarily for post-TRT HPTA restart and natural testosterone optimization.
Community dosing: 100–200 mcg SC daily or 5×/week; upper community ceiling ~300 mcg/day

Regarded as a clean LH stimulator that does not suppress endogenous production. Consistent complaints: variable individual response, short half-life requiring precise timing, and confusion with kisspeptin-54.

Anecdotal libido improvement consistent with testosterone rise over 2–4 weeks

Science confirms strong acute LH stimulation and tachyphylaxis risk. Community application for post-TRT recovery is biologically plausible but not formally studied. No study has tested the community's injection doses. Tachyphylaxis is documented with twice-daily and continuous exposure; whether once-daily injections need cycling is untested.

Speculative Human studies gave kisspeptin-10 as IV boluses and infusions (PMID 21632807) and as subcutaneous infusions in 15 healthy men (PMID 42549827). None tested daily injections. These tiers follow the community range on this page, 100 to 200 mcg daily with a ceiling near 300 mcg.

The math on this one matters. A 5 mg vial reconstituted with 2 mL bacteriostatic water gives you 2,500 mcg per mL, or 25 mcg per unit on a U-100 insulin syringe. For a 100 mcg dose, you're pulling 4 units. For 125 mcg, pull 5 units. Use BAC water specifically. Sterile water lacks the benzyl alcohol preservative, and given how fast kisspeptin-10 degrades, you want every stability advantage. Plan to use the reconstituted vial within 7 to 10 days, maybe 14 at the outside. Refrigerate immediately after mixing. Timing matters more than usual here. Kisspeptin-10 clears the blood within minutes of an IV dose [2]; no study has reported a half-life for a subcutaneous dose. Most community protocols call for evening dosing, 60 to 90 minutes before bed, at the same time each day. Don't skip the day-7 LH blood draw (30 to 60 minutes post-injection). It tells you whether your vial is active and your receptors are responding.
Cycling Protocol
Off Period

No weeks-long on/off cycle has been tested in people. Before a 2026 infusion trial, FDA's 2024 review found no kisspeptin-10 trial longer than a day. Community protocols run 4 weeks on and 4 off (or 30 days on and 30 off) as a precaution against desensitization. Monitor LH and testosterone to see whether your response holds.
Kisspeptin-10 Cycle

Continuous kisspeptin exposure desensitizes the KISS1R (GPR54) pathway. Twice-daily kisspeptin-54 injections in women with hypothalamic amenorrhea cut the LH rise from 24.0 to 2.5 IU/L by the 14th injection day (PMID 19820030). With kisspeptin-10 in healthy men, the LH response to continuous infusion was gone by day 5 (PMID 42549827). It held for 12 days with daily 8-hour infusions. No trial has tested once-daily injections or a weeks-long on/off cycle. Community cycles of 4 weeks on and 4 off, or 5 days on and 2 off, are a precaution, not a tested regimen.
Diminishing LH response vs. first week: confirm with 30-min post-injection blood draw
Testosterone trending back toward baseline despite continued daily injections
Reduced or absent morning erections that were noticeably improved in weeks 1–2
Subjective sense of diminishing response without protocol changes
Gather supplies: 5 mg kisspeptin-10 vial, 2 mL bacteriostatic water, alcohol swabs, U-100 insulin syringe (28 to 31 gauge, 0.5 inch needle).
Reconstitute by injecting 2 mL BAC water slowly down the inside wall of the vial. Do not shake. Swirl gently until dissolved. This gives 2,500 mcg/mL (25 mcg per unit on a U-100 syringe).
Calculate your dose For 100 mcg, draw 4 units. For 125 mcg, draw 5 units. For 200 mcg, draw 8 units. For 300 mcg, draw 12 units.
Clean the injection site with an alcohol swab Preferred sites: abdominal fat (2 inches from the navel) or anterior thigh. Rotate sites daily.
Pinch the skin and insert the needle at a 45 to 90 degree angle. Inject slowly. Hold for 5 seconds before withdrawing.
Timing: inject in the evening, 60 to 90 minutes before bed, at the same time each day. A steady daily time keeps your day-7 LH check comparable from one cycle to the next.
Store the reconstituted vial refrigerated at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius. Use within 7 to 14 days. Do not freeze reconstituted peptide.
On day 7, get a blood draw for LH at 30 to 60 minutes post-injection to confirm your individual response. Total testosterone at day 14 and day 28 tracks the downstream effect.
Alternative Routes
Subcutaneous injection

Subcutaneous dosing keeps blood levels up longer than IV (in women, PMID 21976724), but no half-life or bioavailability has been measured (FDA 2024 review). The community dose of 100–200 mcg/day isn't based on any measured conversion.
Rotate sites (abdomen, anterior thigh). Use 28–31 gauge, 0.5-inch needle.
Intranasal

12.8 nmol/kg intranasal kisspeptin-54 raised mean peak LH by 4.4 IU/L in healthy men and in hypothalamic amenorrhea patients (PMID 40215751). No SC-to-intranasal conversion established; direct dose comparison not available.

First non-invasive kisspeptin route with confirmed LH stimulation in humans (kisspeptin-54). Requires specific nasal spray formulation (stable 60 days refrigerated in published protocol). Not achievable with standard peptide reconstitution. Monitor for commercial or compounding development.
Intravenous (IV)

IV bolus doses in clinical trials: 0.01–3.0 mcg/kg in men (PMID 21632807) and up to 10 nmol/kg in women (PMID 21976724). In men, 3 mcg/kg raised LH less than 1 mcg/kg (PMID 21632807). Provides immediate peak kinetics; extremely short duration (~4 min half-life).
Reserved for diagnostic testing and clinical research. Self-IV carries unacceptable infection and dosing-error risk.
Works With
Gonadorelin

Sequential HPG axis coverage: KP10 stimulates hypothalamic GnRH neurons; gonadorelin (synthetic GnRH) stimulates pituitary gonadotrophs. Used in post-TRT restart for two-level axis stimulation simultaneously.
100 mcg KP10 + 100 mcg gonadorelin SC daily, same window or staggered 30 min apart
HCG

Three-level PCT stack: KP10 (hypothalamus) + HCG (direct Leydig cell stimulation bypassing hypothalamus and pituitary). Covers all three HPG axis levels. Community commonly pairs these during post-TRT recovery.
KP10 100–150 mcg SC daily + HCG 500–1000 IU SC 2–3×/week; monitor testosterone to avoid over-stimulation
Avoid
GnRH antagonists (cetrorelix, ganirelix)
GnRH antagonists block pituitary GnRH receptors, abolishing the downstream LH response that KP10 depends on. Concurrent use renders kisspeptin-10 pharmacologically inert.
GnRH agonists in continuous-use regimens (leuprolide, goserelin)
Continuous GnRH agonist exposure causes pituitary desensitization. Concurrent KP10 will produce unpredictable and likely suppressed gonadotropin responses.
PT-141 (bremelanotide)

Not dangerous to combine, but mechanistically redundant for libido purposes and from different pharmacological timescales. PT-141 gives rapid CNS arousal (minutes); KP10 provides slow hormonal axis effects (weeks). May cause additive nausea and flushing.
Generic / Research
~$55–$65 per 10 mg vial (research-chemical market range); kits with BAC water ~$135/10 mg
Pricing updated 2026-04-09

The most important safety concern with kisspeptin-10 is receptor desensitization. A study by Jayasena and colleagues [4] documented tachyphylaxis with twice-daily kisspeptin-54 injections in women with hypothalamic amenorrhea. LH response diminished with uninterrupted dosing. Kisspeptin-10 shares the same KISS1R receptor and is subject to the same mechanism. A 2026 randomized study in healthy men saw that pattern with kisspeptin-10 itself [6]. After 5 days of continuous subcutaneous infusion (4 men), LH and FSH were no higher than placebo, though testosterone stayed raised. Daily 8-hour infusions with 16-hour breaks (7 men) kept LH raised for 12 days. This is not a mild inconvenience; under continuous exposure, the peptide can stop raising LH. No trial has tested whether a weeks-long on/off cycle prevents it. The second concern is specific to product quality. Kisspeptin-10 has an in vitro plasma half-life of approximately 55 seconds, destroyed by matrix metalloproteinases. It is one of the most degradation-prone peptides available. A vial shipped without cold-chain integrity, reconstituted too early, or stored beyond 2 weeks may contain little to no active peptide. FDA has listed kisspeptin-10 in 503A Category 2 since September 29, 2023. FDA says Category 2 substances "may present significant safety risks"; for kisspeptin-10 it cites possible immunogenicity and limited safety data. Current supply comes from research-chemical products with variable quality control. Published clinical side effects from controlled studies include headache, nausea, and hot flushes. These appear dose-related and are reported at higher IV doses. At community subcutaneous doses of 100 to 200 mcg daily, user reports of adverse effects are sparse. The community sample size is low, concentrated on specialist boards rather than mainstream peptide forums. One interaction worth flagging: opioid analgesics suppress kisspeptin neuron activity. Chronic opioid use may reduce responsiveness to kisspeptin-10, and opioid-induced hypogonadism already impairs the HPG axis at multiple levels. For hormone-sensitive cancers (breast, prostate, ovarian), acute gonadotropin stimulation from kisspeptin-10 may temporarily spike sex steroid levels. This is a contraindication, not a theoretical concern. Pregnancy is a clear contraindication. Kisspeptin stimulates gonadotropin release that could disrupt early pregnancy hormone balance. Safety in pregnant women has not been studied. Anyone using kisspeptin-10 should stop and consult a physician if persistent headache or nausea develops, if no measurable LH response appears after 14 days of consistent dosing, or if symptoms suggest hormonal excess (gynecomastia, acne flares, mood instability).
Common Issues & Solutions

No measurable LH response after 14 days: Check blood draw timing. Community protocols draw at 30–60 min post-injection, though the subcutaneous LH peak hasn't been timed in men. Likely causes: severe HPG axis suppression (iHH patients respond poorly per published data), degraded peptide from storage failure, or inadequate injection technique. Confirm vial reconstituted in BAC water and stored refrigerated.

Loss of response after initial success: possible KISS1R desensitization (tachyphylaxis), documented with twice-daily kisspeptin-54 [4] and continuous kisspeptin-10 infusion [6]. Community practice is a full washout of about 4 weeks before restarting, or a 5 days on / 2 off weekly pattern. Neither has been tested.
No acute libido or erection effect: Expected: KP10 is not PT-141. It acts via the hormonal axis over 2–4 weeks via testosterone rise, not acute CNS arousal. Wrong tool for on-demand use.

Vial appears inactive / no response at first use: In vitro half-life of KP10 is ~55 seconds: one of the most degradation-prone peptides on the market. Causes: shipping without cold pack, reconstituted too early and stored too long (>2 weeks), or non-sterile water used. Replace the vial with one backed by a verified COA; use BAC water; inject within 7–10 days of reconstitution.

Kisspeptin-10 vs. kisspeptin-54 confusion causing over/underdosing: These are not interchangeable. KP54 half-life ~28 min IV vs. KP10 ~4 min; KP54 produces larger sustained LH pulse. Do not apply KP54 nmol/kg dose directly to KP10: equimolar dose of KP10 will produce a weaker, shorter LH pulse.

Kisspeptin-10: Product Quality medium risk

KP10 is one of the most degradation-prone research peptides: in vitro plasma half-life ~55 seconds, enzymatically destroyed by matrix metalloproteinases. The research chemical market is thin: few brands, limited third-party HPLC/MS testing. No compounding pharmacy access (FDA 503A Category 2 since Sept 2023). Quality depends entirely on batch COA and cold-chain integrity.
Lot-specific HPLC purity certificates ≥98% are the usual benchmark
Store lyophilized vial refrigerated at 2–8°C; reconstituted peptide must stay refrigerated and be used within 7–14 days
Use bacteriostatic water (0.9% benzyl alcohol) for reconstitution: extends stability vs. plain sterile water
Do not freeze reconstituted KP10: freezing accelerates peptide bond hydrolysis
Identity confirmation needs mass spectrometry (MS) verification, not UV absorbance alone

Kisspeptin-10 is classified as a research chemical in the United States. It has no FDA-approved therapeutic indication. FDA has listed kisspeptin-10 in 503A Category 2 since September 29, 2023. FDA says Category 2 substances "may present significant safety risks"; for kisspeptin-10 it cites possible immunogenicity and limited safety data. It was still there on FDA's page on October 6, 2026. FDA scheduled its Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee to discuss kisspeptin-10 on October 29, 2024 (Federal Register 2024-21241). No FDA rule adds it to the 503A bulks list. Current supply is exclusively research-grade product labeled "research purposes only, not for human consumption." Quality varies widely. Lot-specific certificates of analysis with HPLC purity and mass spectrometry identity confirmation are the minimum standard for evaluating a batch. The World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) added kisspeptin and its agonist analogues to its Prohibited List in 2024 (S2.2.1, testosterone-stimulating peptides in males). For male athletes, that class is banned at all times, in and out of competition. Clinical research continues internationally. Kisspeptin-54 (the full-length form) has more advanced clinical trial data, particularly for IVF applications. A 2025 trial gave kisspeptin-54 as a nasal spray and raised LH in humans [7]; kisspeptin-10 has no intranasal data. This content is for informational and research purposes only. It does not constitute medical advice. Consult a qualified healthcare provider before using any research peptide.
Evidence grade: Phase 3 trial (Peptide Evidence Gap, October 2026)

faqs.q: Should I use kisspeptin-10 or kisspeptin-54?
faqs.a: Kisspeptin-10 is the minimal active fragment (10 amino acids); kisspeptin-54 is the full native form with a longer half-life and larger LH pulse. Kisspeptin-54 is also significantly more expensive. They're not interchangeable at the same dose; kisspeptin-54 requires different dosing.

faqs.q: Can I use kisspeptin while on TRT?
faqs.a: Yes. Kisspeptin acts upstream (stimulates GnRH, then LH), so it can trigger endogenous testosterone pulses even while on TRT. The catch is that exogenous testosterone suppresses the HPG axis via negative feedback, reducing kisspeptin's effectiveness. You'll see the full benefit when TRT is reduced or during PCT.

faqs.q: How do I convert the clinical study doses to mcg?
faqs.a: Kisspeptin-10 has a molecular weight of ~1302 Da. For a 75 kg person, 1 nmol/kg equals roughly 98 mcg total. Published 1 mcg/kg maximal-response IV doses translate to about 75 mcg. Those are IV numbers, though. No study has reported subcutaneous bioavailability, so they don't convert directly to an injection dose.

faqs.q: Will daily dosing desensitize the receptors?
faqs.a: It can happen, but once-daily injections haven't been tested. Twice-daily kisspeptin-54 injections in women with hypothalamic amenorrhea cut the LH rise from 24.0 to 2.5 IU/L by day 14 (PMID 19820030). In healthy men, the LH response to continuous subcutaneous kisspeptin-10 infusion was gone by day 5 (PMID 42549827). Daily 8-hour infusions with 16-hour breaks kept LH raised for 12 days. No trial has tested daily injections or a weeks-long on/off cycle. Community users cycle 4 weeks on and 4 weeks off as a precaution; a timed LH blood test shows whether your response is holding.

faqs.q: Is kisspeptin-10 useful for erectile dysfunction like PT-141?
faqs.a: Not in the same way at all. PT-141 activates MC4R receptors in the brain within 30-60 minutes for on-demand arousal. Kisspeptin-10 works through the hormonal axis over days to weeks by raising testosterone and LH. It's not an acute ED treatment. If you're expecting PT-141-like effects, you'll be disappointed.
Kisspeptin-10 typically comes in 5mg vials. Add 2mL of bacteriostatic water to the vial. Use the free calculator for exact syringe units based on your desired dose.

faqs.q: What is the half-life of Kisspeptin-10?
faqs.a: The half-life of Kisspeptin-10 is ~4 min (IV); not measured for SC. This determines how frequently you need to dose for consistent blood levels.

summary: . Kisspeptin-10 is the smallest active fragment of kisspeptin, the peptide that tells your hypothalamus to turn on the reproductive hormone cascade. It binds KISS1R on GnRH neurons, triggering a pulsatile release of LH and FSH from the pituitary. The catch: a plasma half-life around 4 minutes after IV dosing, and documented receptor tachyphylaxis with continuous or twice-daily exposure. IVF trials have tested the longer form, kisspeptin-54, as an egg-maturation trigger. The bodybuilding and TRT recovery community uses it to restart endogenous testosterone production.
